topic: Anchoring: the rigged wheel of 1974 and the first number today (30-second sample)
method: Search summaries of the 1974 Science paper and later replication literature, checked across independent sources; the original paper was not re-opened.

claims.claim: In a 1974 experiment, Tversky and Kahneman used a wheel of fortune rigged to stop only at 10 or 65. Participants then estimated the percentage of UN member countries that are African; the median estimate was 25 after a 10 and 45 after a 65.

sources.title: Tversky, A. & Kahneman, D. (1974) Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases. Science 185(4157):1124-1131
sources.quote: [method and medians as summarised, read 2026-11-12] wheel stopping at 10 or 65; median estimates 25 and 45

sources.title: University College Dublin economics working paper WP2024/07 (summary of the 1974 anchoring experiment)
sources.quote: [search summary 2026-11-12] wheel at 10 or 65 shifted estimates by 20 points

claims.notes: Replication status: robust for factual estimates (C2).

claims.claim: The Many Labs 1 project (Klein et al., 2014) replicated classic anchoring effects across many labs, with effects at least as large as the originals; anchoring is among psychology's best-replicated findings.

sources.title: Klein, R. A. et al. (2014) Investigating variation in replicability: A 'Many Labs' replication project. Social Psychology 45(3):142-152
Judgment and Decision Making 14(4), 2019, pp. 470-487
sources.quote: [search summary] Many Labs showed stronger effects than the original for factual anchoring

claims.claim: For prices and product valuations, anchoring evidence is mixed: replications have been inconsistent, including a failed direct replication of a well-known price-anchoring study.

sources.title: Judgment and Decision Making 14(4), 2019, pp. 470-487
sources.quote: [search summary 2026-11-12] replications of anchoring for product valuations have been inconsistent

contradictions: Retail research reports that advertised reference prices raise perceived discounts (Journal of Marketing Research, 2021).
